subject: OptimoBank evaluation cadence, success criteria & kickoff confirmation
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Angela Cheng <angela.cheng@optimobank.com>, Mike Hale <mike.hale@optimobank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: OptimoBank evaluation cadence, success criteria & kickoff confirmation

Hi Angela / Mike — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before kickoff.

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference as a drop-in inference layer for OptimoBanks fraud-scoring and customer messaging workflows.
- Scope for the trial: two models (fraud-score 1.0, templating v2), sandbox integration to a staging queue, 4-week run with weekly check-ins, and a final readout with business metrics.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm / adjust):
1) Accuracy: no more than 5% regression on existing fraud alert precision at current thresholds.
2) Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 300ms for 1k token requests.
3) Cost: projected per-transaction inference cost <= $0.015 for production-like load.
4) Ops: automated prefix caching cut token spend by >= 18% in pilot traces.

Proposed timeline / cadence:
- Kickoff options: May 17 or May 19 (choose one)
- Week 1: baseline metrics collection + ingest test data
- Weeks 2-3: tuning and guardrails (rate limits, tokenization checks)
- Week 4: stakeholder readout and decision gate
- Weekly check-ins: Thursdays 09:00 PT (30 minutes) — short sync + action items

Owners (initial):
- Redwood AE (commercial lead): Chloe Martin (me) — program coordination, contract follow-up
- Redwood Solutions Eng: Ben Carter — integration, staging deployment, perf tuning
- Redwood Customer Success: Marissa Cole — runbook, acceptance criteria, readout format
- OptimoBank Tech Lead: Angela Cheng — datasets, sandbox credentials, access approvals
- OptimoBank Procurement: procurement@optimobank.com — SOW & PO

Attachments: Ive attached a starter POC success matrix (POC-success-metrics.xlsx) and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MutualActionPlan.docx). Please review and mark any items off.

Asks before we kick off:
- Confirm which kickoff date you prefer (May 17 or May 19).
- Share staging sandbox credentials or IP allowlist window for our infra team.
- Confirm any compliance evidence we need earlier (SOC 2 report, data retention policy).

If that all looks right, Ill lock the cadence and send a DocuSign SOW for signature (small PO to cover reserved slots).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: OptimoBank evaluation cadence, success criteria & kickoff confirmation

Thanks Chloe  good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Kickoff: May 17 works better for our engineering calendar. Please schedule for 10:00 PT if possible.
- Metrics: the latency goal should be 95th percentile < 300ms end-to-end (including network hops) for 1k token requests. For fraud scoring wed also like to track tail throughput (steady state qps target: 250 qps).
- Security/compliance: we will need an initial SOC 2 summary and network allowlist instructions before we provide sandbox credentials. Ive attached an internal checklist (optimo_requirements.pdf).
- Data: we will provide a redacted sample transaction dataset (PII removed) but need details on encryption at rest and in transit for the staging bucket.

On procurement: I looped procurement@optimobank.com. They will process a small not-to-exceed SOW. Please include explicit termination and data-handling language in the SOW.

Thanks Angela — Ben from Redwood SEs here. Quick technical notes and asks so we can hit the latency / throughput targets you outlined.

1) Staging topology: please confirm whether the staging queue will be accessible over the public internet or if we should expect a VPN/peering/IP allowlist. If IP allowlist, send a two-hour maintenance window for testing.
2) Dataset: sample redacted dataset is perfect. Please point to a staging S3/GCS path or share via a secure transfer link. Well run an ingest job to establish a baseline.
3) Perf tuning: well run three load profiles (spike, steady 250 qps, and ramp) and share traces. Ben will own kernel selection and caching config; Marissa will own runbook steps for rollbacks.

Attachment: ingest_playbook.md (short checklist for dataset shape and config).

Hi all  Ive drafted a lightweight weekly cadence and final readout agenda so stakeholders know what to expect. Sharing the checklist below and attaching the full agenda (final-readout-agenda.md).

Weekly Check-in (Thursdays 09:00 PT, 30 min):
- 5 min: quick health + blockers from OptimoBank engineering
- 10 min: perf readout from Redwood (latency, token breakouts, cost burn rate)
- 10 min: action items & owners
- 5 min: risks / decisions needed

Week-by-week:
- Week 1: baseline ingest + connectivity validation
- Week 2: tuning + initial QA of outputs (fraud thresholds)
- Week 3: stress profile and cost projections
- Week 4: stakeholder demo + decision gate (go/no-go)

Final readout agenda (high level):
- Executive summary (business KPIs compared to baseline)
- Technical summary (latency, throughput, failure modes)
- Operational readiness (runbook, SLAs, handoff tasks)
- Contractual next steps (SOW, PO timelines)
